On Friday, July 20, 2018 at 10:35:56 PM UTC-4, Joshua Rosenberg wrote:
> Katharina, thank you for this message; please excuse my delay.
>
> I believe this is a bug. The reason is that when we developed that function we were only specifying three models. I think the ultimate solution (fixing the bug) is fairly straightforward and I'll try to work on it next week. If you want to do this in the meantime, I think you can do the following: use "VVI" as the model name. Also, that is in fact model type 3. What is (for the sake of this function) 1 and 2 correspond (correctly) to model types 1 and 2; model type 3 *in this function* is what is now, correctly model type 6. This is very confusing; I apologize. in short:
>
> To carry out the BLRT for:
> model type 1, use 1
> model type 2, use 2
> model type 3, use "VVI"
> model type 6, use 3
> This should work, though I'll try to fix this soon and will send you a note when I do.
> Josh
>
> On Thursday, July 5, 2018 at 7:42:22 AM UTC-4, Katharina wrote:

> >
> > I try to analyze my data with the tidyLPA package in R. In order to decide on the correct number of profiles for the different models, I ran the LRT for the four models.

messages.subject: Re: Issue with estimate profiles
messages.body_plain:
Steve, sure thing, any time –

The functions that use MPlus (those that end in _mplus) use random starts; see estimate_profiles_mplus for some options you can contro
The functions that use mclust (those that don’t end in _mplus) are initialized by a hierarchical cluster analysis, so there’s only one set of start values (those that are the end-values/estimates from the hierarchical cluster analysis)

HTH!

Josh

messages.subject_clean: Updates to tidyLPA (v. 0.2.0 available for testing)
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I wanted to send a note about some updates to the tidyLPA package. The next version includes a large number of changes (detailed here: ). It will be version 0.2.0. If you have the chance to test and provide feedback on it or to ask any questions, they are welcome. You can install the development version (many of you know how to do this 😊) by running the following lines:

install.packages(“devtools”)

devtools::install_github(“jrosen48/tidyLPA”)

This version will be submitted to CRAN soon. Just send a note to tid...@googlegroups.com with any thoguhts.

Sincerely,

Josh

--

Joshua M. Rosenberg, Ph.D.

Assistant Professor, STEM Education

Dept. of Theory and Practice in Teacher Education

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville

420 Claxton, 1122 Volunteer Boulevard, Knoxville, TN 37996

(865) 974-5973

jmros...@utk.edu

<homepage <http://jmichaelrosenberg.com/>>
